correctness.rationale: For distinct real eigenvalues, the exact projected Gram correction on the orthogonal one-dimensional complement has denominator \((\lambda_2-\lambda_1)(ab-c^2)(a-bt^2)\) and numerator \((\lambda_2-\lambda_1)(ab-c^2)t\). Its unique solved projective update is \(t_+=-t^2(c+bt)/(a+ct)\). For every \(H\) with \((1-\epsilon)I\preceq H\preceq(1+\epsilon)I\), the direction \(Hu\) differs from \(u\) by at most \(\arcsin\epsilon\); the exactly attained one-step supremum is \(r^2(r+\tau)/(1-\tau r)\) with \(\tau=\epsilon/\sqrt{1-\epsilon^2}\). Its ratio to \(r\) is strictly less than one precisely for \(0<r<\rho=\sqrt{(1-\epsilon)/(1+\epsilon)}\), implying contraction even for varying admissible sketches. The diagonal metric with diagonal entries \(1-\epsilon\) and \(1+\epsilon\) has an inconsistent projected correction at equality and divergence toward the other eigendirection from every finite exterior start. Direct projected-equation and rational-envelope identities were separately checked in VERIFY.py. The finite checks do not replace the general proof.

value.rationale: The smallest nontrivial spectral plane is a natural model for the exact correction underlying the 2026 randomized Jacobi–Davidson iteration. The main theorem gives the full, attained robust attraction cone over the stated near-isometric Gram family and precisely quantifies the loss of correction solvability at the optimal boundary. It separates globally reliable attraction, a nontrivial singularity, and convergence to an unintended eigenvector. The dependence on embedding distortion is structurally motivated by the source method; these are neither generic local-error order observations nor arbitrary parameter slices. The claim is explicitly limited to the one-vector restarted exact correction model and does not assert a full eigensolver performance bound.
